comparison_design.note: Each arm reuses the same seed, task manifest, disaster parameters, and navigation policy within a paired run.

damage_threshold_semantics.note: These are distinct metrics; occupying a node with positive damage does not necessarily mean the agent observed danger or entered an impassable node.

definitions.affected_agent: At event time, the event intersects the agent's active planner route or its current node/local adjacent nodes.
definitions.response_scope: Affected-pair response coverage counts only agents in the initial affected_agent set for each event. Responses from agents who learn later through communication or shared memory are counted separately as outside-initial-affected-set responses; they still count in total successful_responses.
definitions.response_delay_scope: mean_response_delay_steps and mean_response_delay_all_agents_steps average all recorded responses. The affected_pairs and outside_initial_affected_set keys report those populations separately. Delay is measured from that agent's first recorded awareness of the event.
definitions.awareness_delay_scope: mean_awareness_delay_steps remains the legacy mean for initially affected agent-event pairs. The explicit all_agents and outside_initial_affected_set fields include later-informed agents. Delays are averaged only over raw records with a non-null awareness_delay_steps value.
definitions.awareness_source_counts: Counts first-awareness records by their recorded source (for example self_observation, teammate_message, or shared_memory). Counts are records, not unique agents.
definitions.awareness: First recorded self-observation, teammate-message delivery, or successful cross-agent shared-memory hazard lookup containing a node attributed to the event.
definitions.planner_success: A known event hazard invalidates the active route, a replacement plan is found, and the active route changes.
definitions.default_policy_response: A safe next-hop choice after event awareness. This is descriptive and does not establish causal route change.
definitions.edge_attribution: The engine reports exact edge IDs. Older/custom event providers may fall back to a single-event graph diff; ambiguous simultaneous-event attribution is omitted.

response_metrics.default_policy_route_change_causality: not established; next-hop changes are descriptive only

travel_time.note: Elapsed per-agent decision steps are used for travel time. Global completion timestamps are reported separately and are not mislabeled as individual travel durations.

makespan.note: Team completion makespan is defined only when every navigator completed. Successful-agent makespan is reported separately for partial-completion runs; unfinished agents are right-censored.

task_throughput.definition: Completed navigator goals divided by observed simulation steps. This is a run-level rate, not a per-agent travel speed.

distance.population: All-navigator total is reported only when every navigator has a valid distance; completed-only total is reported only when every completed navigator has a valid distance.
distance.note: Distance is computed from consecutive recorded path nodes using the simulator's geographic edge-distance function when an explicit distance counter is unavailable. Per-agent values may be present even when a population total is incomplete.

sensing_neighborhood_exposure.definition: An agent is counted once per step when a damaged node or disabled edge is in its current-node/one-hop sensing neighbourhood. This is proximity exposure, not physical contact.

severity_weighted_exposure.definition: For each observed agent-step, the maximum node-damage severity in the current node plus one-hop neighbourhood, summed over observed agent-steps. The observed-agent-step mean includes zero-severity observations; the positive-severity mean excludes them. This is a proximity-weighted dose proxy, not a physiological dose or physical-contact measure.

hazard_exposure.severity_weighted_exposure_note: Uses simulator-recorded per-agent, per-step local maximum node damage. Compare only under identical sensing/neighbourhood definitions and simulation horizons.

navigation_association_not_causation.interpretation: Default-policy next-hop changes after information are temporal associations, not causal proof. Planner route changes retain the existing known-blocked-route trigger.

useful_information.raw_read_level_definition: Repeated successful hazard reads are counted; this is access activity, not a count of distinct information acquisitions.
useful_information.usefulness_definition: Unique route-relevant recipient-node acquisitions divided by all unique cross-agent recipient-node acquisitions; deduplicated across shared-memory and local-message channels. Event-level counts are also reported when event mappings exist.
useful_information.interpretation: Route relevance is a snapshot at first cross-agent arrival. Acquisition and novelty are instrumentation proxies, not proof that the agent causally used the information or improved an outcome. Raw repeated reads remain separately available.

communication_efficiency.zero_denominator_policy: Undefined ratios are null, never zero or infinity.

pheromone.interpretation: The no-pheromone counterfactual holds the candidate set and selection temperature fixed and removes only the pheromone score term. Argmax changes show direct score-ranking influence; probability effects quantify the change in candidate selection probability. These are per-decision policy counterfactuals, not a substitute for the paired pheromone-off experiment.

scaling_efficiency.note: A single run cannot establish scaling efficiency. Compare matched workloads at multiple agent counts, then compute throughput(N)/[N * throughput(1)] or an explicitly chosen speedup/efficiency measure across those runs.

definitions.planner_success: A known event hazard invalidates the active route, a replacement plan is found, and the active route changes.
definitions.default_policy_response: A safe next-hop choice after event awareness. This is descriptive and does not establish causal route change.

travel_time.note: Elapsed per-agent decision steps are used for travel time. Global completion timestamps are reported separately and are not mislabeled as individual travel durations.

makespan.note: Team completion makespan is defined only when every navigator completed. Successful-agent makespan is reported separately for partial-completion runs; unfinished agents are right-censored.

task_throughput.definition: Completed navigator goals divided by observed simulation steps. This is a run-level rate, not a per-agent travel speed.

distance.population: All-navigator total is reported only when every navigator has a valid distance; completed-only total is reported only when every completed navigator has a valid distance.
distance.note: Distance is computed from consecutive recorded path nodes using the simulator's geographic edge-distance function when an explicit distance counter is unavailable. Per-agent values may be present even when a population total is incomplete.

sensing_neighborhood_exposure.definition: An agent is counted once per step when a damaged node or disabled edge is in its current-node/one-hop sensing neighbourhood. This is proximity exposure, not physical contact.

severity_weighted_exposure.definition: For each observed agent-step, the maximum node-damage severity in the current node plus one-hop neighbourhood, summed over observed agent-steps. The observed-agent-step mean includes zero-severity observations; the positive-severity mean excludes them. This is a proximity-weighted dose proxy, not a physiological dose or physical-contact measure.

hazard_exposure.severity_weighted_exposure_note: Uses simulator-recorded per-agent, per-step local maximum node damage. Compare only under identical sensing/neighbourhood definitions and simulation horizons.

navigation_association_not_causation.interpretation: Default-policy next-hop changes after information are temporal associations, not causal proof. Planner route changes retain the existing known-blocked-route trigger.

useful_information.raw_read_level_definition: Repeated successful hazard reads are counted; this is access activity, not a count of distinct information acquisitions.
useful_information.usefulness_definition: Unique route-relevant recipient-node acquisitions divided by all unique cross-agent recipient-node acquisitions; deduplicated across shared-memory and local-message channels. Event-level counts are also reported when event mappings exist.
useful_information.interpretation: Route relevance is a snapshot at first cross-agent arrival. Acquisition and novelty are instrumentation proxies, not proof that the agent causally used the information or improved an outcome. Raw repeated reads remain separately available.

communication_efficiency.zero_denominator_policy: Undefined ratios are null, never zero or infinity.

pheromone.interpretation: The no-pheromone counterfactual holds the candidate set and selection temperature fixed and removes only the pheromone score term. scaling_efficiency.note: A single run cannot establish scaling efficiency. Compare matched workloads at multiple agent counts, then compute throughput(N)/[N * throughput(1)] or an explicitly chosen speedup/efficiency measure across those runs.

makespan.note: Team completion makespan is defined only when every navigator completed. Successful-agent makespan is reported separately for partial-completion runs; unfinished agents are right-censored.

task_throughput.definition: Completed navigator goals divided by observed simulation steps. This is a run-level rate, not a per-agent travel speed.

distance.population: All-navigator total is reported only when every navigator has a valid distance; completed-only total is reported only when every completed navigator has a valid distance.
distance.note: Distance is computed from consecutive recorded path nodes using the simulator's geographic edge-distance function when an explicit distance counter is unavailable. Per-agent values may be present even when a population total is incomplete.

sensing_neighborhood_exposure.definition: An agent is counted once per step when a damaged node or disabled edge is in its current-node/one-hop sensing neighbourhood. This is proximity exposure, not physical contact.

severity_weighted_exposure.definition: For each observed agent-step, the maximum node-damage severity in the current node plus one-hop neighbourhood, summed over observed agent-steps. The observed-agent-step mean includes zero-severity observations; the positive-severity mean excludes them. This is a proximity-weighted dose proxy, not a physiological dose or physical-contact measure.

hazard_exposure.severity_weighted_exposure_note: Uses simulator-recorded per-agent, per-step local maximum node damage. Compare only under identical sensing/neighbourhood definitions and simulation horizons.

navigation_association_not_causation.interpretation: Default-policy next-hop changes after information are temporal associations, not causal proof. Planner route changes retain the existing known-blocked-route trigger.

useful_information.raw_read_level_definition: Repeated successful hazard reads are counted; this is access activity, not a count of distinct information acquisitions.
useful_information.usefulness_definition: Unique route-relevant recipient-node acquisitions divided by all unique cross-agent recipient-node acquisitions; deduplicated across shared-memory and local-message channels. Event-level counts are also reported when event mappings exist.
useful_information.interpretation: Route relevance is a snapshot at first cross-agent arrival. Acquisition and novelty are instrumentation proxies, not proof that the agent causally used the information or improved an outcome. Raw repeated reads remain separately available.

communication_efficiency.zero_denominator_policy: Undefined ratios are null, never zero or infinity.

pheromone.interpretation: The no-pheromone counterfactual holds the candidate set and selection temperature fixed and removes only the pheromone score term. Argmax changes show direct score-ranking influence; probability effects quantify the change in candidate selection probability. These are per-decision policy counterfactuals, not a substitute for the paired pheromone-off experiment.

scaling_efficiency.note: A single run cannot establish scaling efficiency. Compare matched workloads at multiple agent counts, then compute throughput(N)/[N * throughput(1)] or an explicitly chosen speedup/efficiency measure across those runs.

The observed-agent-step mean includes zero-severity observations; the positive-severity mean excludes them. hazard_exposure.severity_weighted_exposure_note: Uses simulator-recorded per-agent, per-step local maximum node damage. Compare only under identical sensing/neighbourhood definitions and simulation horizons.

navigation_association_not_causation.interpretation: Default-policy next-hop changes after information are temporal associations, not causal proof. Planner route changes retain the existing known-blocked-route trigger.

useful_information.raw_read_level_definition: Repeated successful hazard reads are counted; this is access activity, not a count of distinct information acquisitions.
useful_information.usefulness_definition: Unique route-relevant recipient-node acquisitions divided by all unique cross-agent recipient-node acquisitions; deduplicated across shared-memory and local-message channels. Event-level counts are also reported when event mappings exist.
useful_information.interpretation: Route relevance is a snapshot at first cross-agent arrival. Acquisition and novelty are instrumentation proxies, not proof that the agent causally used the information or improved an outcome. Raw repeated reads remain separately available.

communication_efficiency.zero_denominator_policy: Undefined ratios are null, never zero or infinity.

pheromone.interpretation: The no-pheromone counterfactual holds the candidate set and selection temperature fixed and removes only the pheromone score term. scaling_efficiency.note: A single run cannot establish scaling efficiency. Compare matched workloads at multiple agent counts, then compute throughput(N)/[N * throughput(1)] or an explicitly chosen speedup/efficiency measure across those runs.

sensing_neighborhood_exposure.definition: An agent is counted once per step when a damaged node or disabled edge is in its current-node/one-hop sensing neighbourhood. This is proximity exposure, not physical contact.

definitions.affected_agent: At event time, the event intersects the agent's active planner route or its current node/local adjacent nodes.
definitions.response_scope: Affected-pair response coverage counts only agents in the initial affected_agent set for each event. definitions.response_delay_scope: mean_response_delay_steps and mean_response_delay_all_agents_steps average all recorded responses. definitions.awareness_source_counts: Counts first-awareness records by their recorded source (for example self_observation, teammate_message, or shared_memory). Counts are records, not unique agents.
definitions.awareness: First recorded self-observation, teammate-message delivery, or successful cross-agent shared-memory hazard lookup containing a node attributed to the event.
definitions.planner_success: A known event hazard invalidates the active route, a replacement plan is found, and the active route changes.

response_metrics.default_policy_route_change_causality: not established; next-hop changes are descriptive only

travel_time.note: Elapsed per-agent decision steps are used for travel time. Global completion timestamps are reported separately and are not mislabeled as individual travel durations.

makespan.note: Team completion makespan is defined only when every navigator completed. Successful-agent makespan is reported separately for partial-completion runs; unfinished agents are right-censored.

task_throughput.definition: Completed navigator goals divided by observed simulation steps. This is a run-level rate, not a per-agent travel speed.

distance.population: All-navigator total is reported only when every navigator has a valid distance; completed-only total is reported only when every completed navigator has a valid distance.
distance.note: Distance is computed from consecutive recorded path nodes using the simulator's geographic edge-distance function when an explicit distance counter is unavailable. Per-agent values may be present even when a population total is incomplete.

sensing_neighborhood_exposure.definition: An agent is counted once per step when a damaged node or disabled edge is in its current-node/one-hop sensing neighbourhood. This is proximity exposure, not physical contact.

severity_weighted_exposure.definition: For each observed agent-step, the maximum node-damage severity in the current node plus one-hop neighbourhood, summed over observed agent-steps. The observed-agent-step mean includes zero-severity observations; the positive-severity mean excludes them. This is a proximity-weighted dose proxy, not a physiological dose or physical-contact measure.

hazard_exposure.severity_weighted_exposure_note: Uses simulator-recorded per-agent, per-step local maximum node damage. Compare only under identical sensing/neighbourhood definitions and simulation horizons.

navigation_association_not_causation.interpretation: Default-policy next-hop changes after information are temporal associations, not causal proof. Planner route changes retain the existing known-blocked-route trigger.

useful_information.raw_read_level_definition: Repeated successful hazard reads are counted; this is access activity, not a count of distinct information acquisitions.

useful_information.interpretation: Route relevance is a snapshot at first cross-agent arrival. Acquisition and novelty are instrumentation proxies, not proof that the agent causally used the information or improved an outcome. Raw repeated reads remain separately available.

communication_efficiency.zero_denominator_policy: Undefined ratios are null, never zero or infinity.

pheromone.interpretation: The no-pheromone counterfactual holds the candidate set and selection temperature fixed and removes only the pheromone score term. definitions.edge_attribution: The engine reports exact edge IDs. Older/custom event providers may fall back to a single-event graph diff; ambiguous simultaneous-event attribution is omitted.

response_metrics.default_policy_route_change_causality: not established; next-hop changes are descriptive only

travel_time.note: Elapsed per-agent decision steps are used for travel time. Global completion timestamps are reported separately and are not mislabeled as individual travel durations.

makespan.note: Team completion makespan is defined only when every navigator completed. Successful-agent makespan is reported separately for partial-completion runs; unfinished agents are right-censored.

task_throughput.definition: Completed navigator goals divided by observed simulation steps. This is a run-level rate, not a per-agent travel speed.

distance.population: All-navigator total is reported only when every navigator has a valid distance; completed-only total is reported only when every completed navigator has a valid distance.
distance.note: Distance is computed from consecutive recorded path nodes using the simulator's geographic edge-distance function when an explicit distance counter is unavailable. Per-agent values may be present even when a population total is incomplete.

sensing_neighborhood_exposure.definition: An agent is counted once per step when a damaged node or disabled edge is in its current-node/one-hop sensing neighbourhood. This is proximity exposure, not physical contact.

severity_weighted_exposure.definition: For each observed agent-step, the maximum node-damage severity in the current node plus one-hop neighbourhood, summed over observed agent-steps. The observed-agent-step mean includes zero-severity observations; the positive-severity mean excludes them. This is a proximity-weighted dose proxy, not a physiological dose or physical-contact measure.

hazard_exposure.severity_weighted_exposure_note: Uses simulator-recorded per-agent, per-step local maximum node damage. Compare only under identical sensing/neighbourhood definitions and simulation horizons.

navigation_association_not_causation.interpretation: Default-policy next-hop changes after information are temporal associations, not causal proof. Planner route changes retain the existing known-blocked-route trigger.

useful_information.raw_read_level_definition: Repeated successful hazard reads are counted; this is access activity, not a count of distinct information acquisitions.
useful_information.usefulness_definition: Unique route-relevant recipient-node acquisitions divided by all unique cross-agent recipient-node acquisitions; deduplicated across shared-memory and local-message channels. Event-level counts are also reported when event mappings exist.
useful_information.interpretation: Route relevance is a snapshot at first cross-agent arrival. Acquisition and novelty are instrumentation proxies, not proof that the agent causally used the information or improved an outcome. Raw repeated reads remain separately available.

communication_efficiency.zero_denominator_policy: Undefined ratios are null, never zero or infinity.

pheromone.interpretation: The no-pheromone counterfactual holds the candidate set and selection temperature fixed and removes only the pheromone score term. Argmax changes show direct score-ranking influence; probability effects quantify the change in candidate selection probability. These are per-decision policy counterfactuals, not a substitute for the paired pheromone-off experiment.

scaling_efficiency.note: A single run cannot establish scaling efficiency. Compare matched workloads at multiple agent counts, then compute throughput(N)/[N * throughput(1)] or an explicitly chosen speedup/efficiency measure across those runs.

definitions.affected_agent: At event time, the event intersects the agent's active planner route or its current node/local adjacent nodes.
definitions.response_scope: Affected-pair response coverage counts only agents in the initial affected_agent set for each event. Responses from agents who learn later through communication or shared memory are counted separately as outside-initial-affected-set responses; they still count in total successful_responses.
definitions.response_delay_scope: mean_response_delay_steps and mean_response_delay_all_agents_steps average all recorded responses. The affected_pairs and outside_initial_affected_set keys report those populations separately. Delay is measured from that agent's first recorded awareness of the event.
definitions.awareness_delay_scope: mean_awareness_delay_steps remains the legacy mean for initially affected agent-event pairs. The explicit all_agents and outside_initial_affected_set fields include later-informed agents. Delays are averaged only over raw records with a non-null awareness_delay_steps value.
definitions.awareness_source_counts: Counts first-awareness records by their recorded source (for example self_observation, teammate_message, or shared_memory). Counts are records, not unique agents.
definitions.awareness: First recorded self-observation, teammate-message delivery, or successful cross-agent shared-memory hazard lookup containing a node attributed to the event.
definitions.planner_success: A known event hazard invalidates the active route, a replacement plan is found, and the active route changes.
definitions.default_policy_response: A safe next-hop choice after event awareness. This is descriptive and does not establish causal route change.
definitions.edge_attribution: The engine reports exact edge IDs. Older/custom event providers may fall back to a single-event graph diff; ambiguous simultaneous-event attribution is omitted.

response_metrics.default_policy_route_change_causality: not established; next-hop changes are descriptive only

travel_time.note: Elapsed per-agent decision steps are used for travel time. Global completion timestamps are reported separately and are not mislabeled as individual travel durations.

makespan.note: Team completion makespan is defined only when every navigator completed. Successful-agent makespan is reported separately for partial-completion runs; unfinished agents are right-censored.

task_throughput.definition: Completed navigator goals divided by observed simulation steps. This is a run-level rate, not a per-agent travel speed.

distance.population: All-navigator total is reported only when every navigator has a valid distance; completed-only total is reported only when every completed navigator has a valid distance.
distance.note: Distance is computed from consecutive recorded path nodes using the simulator's geographic edge-distance function when an explicit distance counter is unavailable. Per-agent values may be present even when a population total is incomplete.

sensing_neighborhood_exposure.definition: An agent is counted once per step when a damaged node or disabled edge is in its current-node/one-hop sensing neighbourhood. This is proximity exposure, not physical contact.

severity_weighted_exposure.definition: For each observed agent-step, the maximum node-damage severity in the current node plus one-hop neighbourhood, summed over observed agent-steps. The observed-agent-step mean includes zero-severity observations; the positive-severity mean excludes them. This is a proximity-weighted dose proxy, not a physiological dose or physical-contact measure.

hazard_exposure.severity_weighted_exposure_note: Uses simulator-recorded per-agent, per-step local maximum node damage. Compare only under identical sensing/neighbourhood definitions and simulation horizons.

navigation_association_not_causation.interpretation: Default-policy next-hop changes after information are temporal associations, not causal proof. Planner route changes retain the existing known-blocked-route trigger.

useful_information.raw_read_level_definition: Repeated successful hazard reads are counted; this is access activity, not a count of distinct information acquisitions.
useful_information.usefulness_definition: Unique route-relevant recipient-node acquisitions divided by all unique cross-agent recipient-node acquisitions; deduplicated across shared-memory and local-message channels. Event-level counts are also reported when event mappings exist.
useful_information.interpretation: Route relevance is a snapshot at first cross-agent arrival. Acquisition and novelty are instrumentation proxies, not proof that the agent causally used the information or improved an outcome. Raw repeated reads remain separately available.

communication_efficiency.zero_denominator_policy: Undefined ratios are null, never zero or infinity.

pheromone.interpretation: The no-pheromone counterfactual holds the candidate set and selection temperature fixed and removes only the pheromone score term. Argmax changes show direct score-ranking influence; probability effects quantify the change in candidate selection probability. These are per-decision policy counterfactuals, not a substitute for the paired pheromone-off experiment.

scaling_efficiency.note: A single run cannot establish scaling efficiency. Compare matched workloads at multiple agent counts, then compute throughput(N)/[N * throughput(1)] or an explicitly chosen speedup/efficiency measure across those runs.

Responses from agents who learn later through communication or shared memory are counted separately as outside-initial-affected-set responses; they still count in total successful_responses.
definitions.response_delay_scope: mean_response_delay_steps and mean_response_delay_all_agents_steps average all recorded responses. The affected_pairs and outside_initial_affected_set keys report those populations separately. Delay is measured from that agent's first recorded awareness of the event.
definitions.awareness_delay_scope: mean_awareness_delay_steps remains the legacy mean for initially affected agent-event pairs. The explicit all_agents and outside_initial_affected_set fields include later-informed agents. Delays are averaged only over raw records with a non-null awareness_delay_steps value.
definitions.awareness_source_counts: Counts first-awareness records by their recorded source (for example self_observation, teammate_message, or shared_memory). Counts are records, not unique agents.
definitions.awareness: First recorded self-observation, teammate-message delivery, or successful cross-agent shared-memory hazard lookup containing a node attributed to the event.
definitions.planner_success: A known event hazard invalidates the active route, a replacement plan is found, and the active route changes.
definitions.default_policy_response: A safe next-hop choice after event awareness. This is descriptive and does not establish causal route change.
definitions.edge_attribution: The engine reports exact edge IDs. Older/custom event providers may fall back to a single-event graph diff; ambiguous simultaneous-event attribution is omitted.

response_metrics.default_policy_route_change_causality: not established; next-hop changes are descriptive only

travel_time.note: Elapsed per-agent decision steps are used for travel time. Global completion timestamps are reported separately and are not mislabeled as individual travel durations.

makespan.note: Team completion makespan is defined only when every navigator completed. Successful-agent makespan is reported separately for partial-completion runs; unfinished agents are right-censored.

task_throughput.definition: Completed navigator goals divided by observed simulation steps. This is a run-level rate, not a per-agent travel speed.

distance.population: All-navigator total is reported only when every navigator has a valid distance; completed-only total is reported only when every completed navigator has a valid distance.
distance.note: Distance is computed from consecutive recorded path nodes using the simulator's geographic edge-distance function when an explicit distance counter is unavailable. Per-agent values may be present even when a population total is incomplete.

sensing_neighborhood_exposure.definition: An agent is counted once per step when a damaged node or disabled edge is in its current-node/one-hop sensing neighbourhood. This is proximity exposure, not physical contact.

severity_weighted_exposure.definition: For each observed agent-step, the maximum node-damage severity in the current node plus one-hop neighbourhood, summed over observed agent-steps. The observed-agent-step mean includes zero-severity observations; the positive-severity mean excludes them. This is a proximity-weighted dose proxy, not a physiological dose or physical-contact measure.

hazard_exposure.severity_weighted_exposure_note: Uses simulator-recorded per-agent, per-step local maximum node damage. Compare only under identical sensing/neighbourhood definitions and simulation horizons.

navigation_association_not_causation.interpretation: Default-policy next-hop changes after information are temporal associations, not causal proof. Planner route changes retain the existing known-blocked-route trigger.

useful_information.raw_read_level_definition: Repeated successful hazard reads are counted; this is access activity, not a count of distinct information acquisitions.
useful_information.usefulness_definition: Unique route-relevant recipient-node acquisitions divided by all unique cross-agent recipient-node acquisitions; deduplicated across shared-memory and local-message channels. Event-level counts are also reported when event mappings exist.
useful_information.interpretation: Route relevance is a snapshot at first cross-agent arrival. Acquisition and novelty are instrumentation proxies, not proof that the agent causally used the information or improved an outcome. Raw repeated reads remain separately available.

communication_efficiency.zero_denominator_policy: Undefined ratios are null, never zero or infinity.

pheromone.interpretation: The no-pheromone counterfactual holds the candidate set and selection temperature fixed and removes only the pheromone score term. Argmax changes show direct score-ranking influence; probability effects quantify the change in candidate selection probability. These are per-decision policy counterfactuals, not a substitute for the paired pheromone-off experiment.

scaling_efficiency.note: A single run cannot establish scaling efficiency. Compare matched workloads at multiple agent counts, then compute throughput(N)/[N * throughput(1)] or an explicitly chosen speedup/efficiency measure across those runs.

instrumentation_notes.coverage: Exact visited node-ID sets and cell-count keys.
instrumentation_notes.awareness: One first-awareness record per agent-event pair.
instrumentation_notes.early_warning: Censored if the agent never independently discovers the event.
instrumentation_notes.travel_time: Per-agent decision steps for completed navigators; global completion timestamps reported separately.
instrumentation_notes.makespan: Team completion makespan is null unless all navigators complete; partial successful makespan and observed horizon are separate.

instrumentation_notes.scaling: Cross-agent-count efficiency requires matched runs at multiple agent counts.
instrumentation_notes.causality: Post-awareness navigation changes are not automatically causal.

damage_threshold_semantics.note: These are distinct metrics; occupying a node with positive damage does not necessarily mean the agent observed danger or entered an impassable node.

definitions.planner_success: A known event hazard invalidates the active route, a replacement plan is found, and the active route changes.
definitions.default_policy_response: A safe next-hop choice after event awareness. This is descriptive and does not establish causal route change.
definitions.edge_attribution: The engine reports exact edge IDs. Older/custom event providers may fall back to a single-event graph diff; ambiguous simultaneous-event attribution is omitted.

response_metrics.default_policy_route_change_causality: not established; next-hop changes are descriptive only

travel_time.note: Elapsed per-agent decision steps are used for travel time. Global completion timestamps are reported separately and are not mislabeled as individual travel durations.

makespan.note: Team completion makespan is defined only when every navigator completed. Successful-agent makespan is reported separately for partial-completion runs; unfinished agents are right-censored.

task_throughput.definition: Completed navigator goals divided by observed simulation steps. This is a run-level rate, not a per-agent travel speed.

distance.population: All-navigator total is reported only when every navigator has a valid distance; completed-only total is reported only when every completed navigator has a valid distance.
distance.note: Distance is computed from consecutive recorded path nodes using the simulator's geographic edge-distance function when an explicit distance counter is unavailable. Per-agent values may be present even when a population total is incomplete.

sensing_neighborhood_exposure.definition: An agent is counted once per step when a damaged node or disabled edge is in its current-node/one-hop sensing neighbourhood. This is proximity exposure, not physical contact.

severity_weighted_exposure.definition: For each observed agent-step, the maximum node-damage severity in the current node plus one-hop neighbourhood, summed over observed agent-steps. The observed-agent-step mean includes zero-severity observations; the positive-severity mean excludes them. This is a proximity-weighted dose proxy, not a physiological dose or physical-contact measure.

hazard_exposure.severity_weighted_exposure_note: Uses simulator-recorded per-agent, per-step local maximum node damage. Compare only under identical sensing/neighbourhood definitions and simulation horizons.

navigation_association_not_causation.interpretation: Default-policy next-hop changes after information are temporal associations, not causal proof. Planner route changes retain the existing known-blocked-route trigger.

useful_information.raw_read_level_definition: Repeated successful hazard reads are counted; this is access activity, not a count of distinct information acquisitions.
useful_information.usefulness_definition: Unique route-relevant recipient-node acquisitions divided by all unique cross-agent recipient-node acquisitions; deduplicated across shared-memory and local-message channels. Event-level counts are also reported when event mappings exist.
useful_information.interpretation: Route relevance is a snapshot at first cross-agent arrival. Acquisition and novelty are instrumentation proxies, not proof that the agent causally used the information or improved an outcome. Raw repeated reads remain separately available.

communication_efficiency.zero_denominator_policy: Undefined ratios are null, never zero or infinity.

pheromone.interpretation: The no-pheromone counterfactual holds the candidate set and selection temperature fixed and removes only the pheromone score term. Argmax changes show direct score-ranking influence; probability effects quantify the change in candidate selection probability. These are per-decision policy counterfactuals, not a substitute for the paired pheromone-off experiment.

scaling_efficiency.note: A single run cannot establish scaling efficiency. Compare matched workloads at multiple agent counts, then compute throughput(N)/[N * throughput(1)] or an explicitly chosen speedup/efficiency measure across those runs.

task_throughput.definition: Completed navigator goals divided by observed simulation steps. This is a run-level rate, not a per-agent travel speed.

distance.population: All-navigator total is reported only when every navigator has a valid distance; completed-only total is reported only when every completed navigator has a valid distance.
distance.note: Distance is computed from consecutive recorded path nodes using the simulator's geographic edge-distance function when an explicit distance counter is unavailable. Per-agent values may be present even when a population total is incomplete.

sensing_neighborhood_exposure.definition: An agent is counted once per step when a damaged node or disabled edge is in its current-node/one-hop sensing neighbourhood. This is proximity exposure, not physical contact.

severity_weighted_exposure.definition: For each observed agent-step, the maximum node-damage severity in the current node plus one-hop neighbourhood, summed over observed agent-steps. The observed-agent-step mean includes zero-severity observations; the positive-severity mean excludes them. This is a proximity-weighted dose proxy, not a physiological dose or physical-contact measure.

hazard_exposure.severity_weighted_exposure_note: Uses simulator-recorded per-agent, per-step local maximum node damage. Compare only under identical sensing/neighbourhood definitions and simulation horizons.

navigation_association_not_causation.interpretation: Default-policy next-hop changes after information are temporal associations, not causal proof. Planner route changes retain the existing known-blocked-route trigger.

useful_information.raw_read_level_definition: Repeated successful hazard reads are counted; this is access activity, not a count of distinct information acquisitions.
useful_information.usefulness_definition: Unique route-relevant recipient-node acquisitions divided by all unique cross-agent recipient-node acquisitions; deduplicated across shared-memory and local-message channels. Event-level counts are also reported when event mappings exist.
useful_information.interpretation: Route relevance is a snapshot at first cross-agent arrival. Acquisition and novelty are instrumentation proxies, not proof that the agent causally used the information or improved an outcome. Raw repeated reads remain separately available.

communication_efficiency.zero_denominator_policy: Undefined ratios are null, never zero or infinity.

pheromone.interpretation: The no-pheromone counterfactual holds the candidate set and selection temperature fixed and removes only the pheromone score term. Argmax changes show direct score-ranking influence; probability effects quantify the change in candidate selection probability. scaling_efficiency.note: A single run cannot establish scaling efficiency. Compare matched workloads at multiple agent counts, then compute throughput(N)/[N * throughput(1)] or an explicitly chosen speedup/efficiency measure across those runs.

definitions.affected_agent: At event time, the event intersects the agent's active planner route or its current node/local adjacent nodes.
definitions.response_scope: Affected-pair response coverage counts only agents in the initial affected_agent set for each event. Responses from agents who learn later through communication or shared memory are counted separately as outside-initial-affected-set responses; they still count in total successful_responses.
definitions.response_delay_scope: mean_response_delay_steps and mean_response_delay_all_agents_steps average all recorded responses. The affected_pairs and outside_initial_affected_set keys report those populations separately. Delay is measured from that agent's first recorded awareness of the event.
definitions.awareness_delay_scope: mean_awareness_delay_steps remains the legacy mean for initially affected agent-event pairs. The explicit all_agents and outside_initial_affected_set fields include later-informed agents. Delays are averaged only over raw records with a non-null awareness_delay_steps value.
definitions.awareness_source_counts: Counts first-awareness records by their recorded source (for example self_observation, teammate_message, or shared_memory). Counts are records, not unique agents.
definitions.awareness: First recorded self-observation, teammate-message delivery, or successful cross-agent shared-memory hazard lookup containing a node attributed to the event.
definitions.planner_success: A known event hazard invalidates the active route, a replacement plan is found, and the active route changes.
definitions.default_policy_response: A safe next-hop choice after event awareness. This is descriptive and does not establish causal route change.
definitions.edge_attribution: The engine reports exact edge IDs. Older/custom event providers may fall back to a single-event graph diff; ambiguous simultaneous-event attribution is omitted.

response_metrics.default_policy_route_change_causality: not established; next-hop changes are descriptive only

travel_time.note: Elapsed per-agent decision steps are used for travel time. Global completion timestamps are reported separately and are not mislabeled as individual travel durations.

makespan.note: Team completion makespan is defined only when every navigator completed. Successful-agent makespan is reported separately for partial-completion runs; unfinished agents are right-censored.

task_throughput.definition: Completed navigator goals divided by observed simulation steps. This is a run-level rate, not a per-agent travel speed.

distance.population: All-navigator total is reported only when every navigator has a valid distance; completed-only total is reported only when every completed navigator has a valid distance.
distance.note: Distance is computed from consecutive recorded path nodes using the simulator's geographic edge-distance function when an explicit distance counter is unavailable. Per-agent values may be present even when a population total is incomplete.

sensing_neighborhood_exposure.definition: An agent is counted once per step when a damaged node or disabled edge is in its current-node/one-hop sensing neighbourhood. This is proximity exposure, not physical contact.

severity_weighted_exposure.definition: For each observed agent-step, the maximum node-damage severity in the current node plus one-hop neighbourhood, summed over observed agent-steps. The observed-agent-step mean includes zero-severity observations; the positive-severity mean excludes them. This is a proximity-weighted dose proxy, not a physiological dose or physical-contact measure.

hazard_exposure.severity_weighted_exposure_note: Uses simulator-recorded per-agent, per-step local maximum node damage. Compare only under identical sensing/neighbourhood definitions and simulation horizons.

navigation_association_not_causation.interpretation: Default-policy next-hop changes after information are temporal associations, not causal proof. Planner route changes retain the existing known-blocked-route trigger.

useful_information.raw_read_level_definition: Repeated successful hazard reads are counted; this is access activity, not a count of distinct information acquisitions.
useful_information.usefulness_definition: Unique route-relevant recipient-node acquisitions divided by all unique cross-agent recipient-node acquisitions; deduplicated across shared-memory and local-message channels. Event-level counts are also reported when event mappings exist.
useful_information.interpretation: Route relevance is a snapshot at first cross-agent arrival. Acquisition and novelty are instrumentation proxies, not proof that the agent causally used the information or improved an outcome. Raw repeated reads remain separately available.

communication_efficiency.zero_denominator_policy: Undefined ratios are null, never zero or infinity.

pheromone.interpretation: The no-pheromone counterfactual holds the candidate set and selection temperature fixed and removes only the pheromone score term. Argmax changes show direct score-ranking influence; probability effects quantify the change in candidate selection probability. These are per-decision policy counterfactuals, not a substitute for the paired pheromone-off experiment.

scaling_efficiency.note: A single run cannot establish scaling efficiency. Compare matched workloads at multiple agent counts, then compute throughput(N)/[N * throughput(1)] or an explicitly chosen speedup/efficiency measure across those runs.

definitions.affected_agent: At event time, the event intersects the agent's active planner route or its current node/local adjacent nodes.
definitions.response_scope: Affected-pair response coverage counts only agents in the initial affected_agent set for each event. Responses from agents who learn later through communication or shared memory are counted separately as outside-initial-affected-set responses; they still count in total successful_responses.
definitions.response_delay_scope: mean_response_delay_steps and mean_response_delay_all_agents_steps average all recorded responses. The affected_pairs and outside_initial_affected_set keys report those populations separately. Delay is measured from that agent's first recorded awareness of the event.
definitions.awareness_delay_scope: mean_awareness_delay_steps remains the legacy mean for initially affected agent-event pairs. The explicit all_agents and outside_initial_affected_set fields include later-informed agents. Delays are averaged only over raw records with a non-null awareness_delay_steps value.
definitions.awareness_source_counts: Counts first-awareness records by their recorded source (for example self_observation, teammate_message, or shared_memory). Counts are records, not unique agents.
definitions.awareness: First recorded self-observation, teammate-message delivery, or successful cross-agent shared-memory hazard lookup containing a node attributed to the event.
definitions.planner_success: A known event hazard invalidates the active route, a replacement plan is found, and the active route changes.
definitions.default_policy_response: A safe next-hop choice after event awareness. This is descriptive and does not establish causal route change.
definitions.edge_attribution: The engine reports exact edge IDs. Older/custom event providers may fall back to a single-event graph diff; ambiguous simultaneous-event attribution is omitted.

response_metrics.default_policy_route_change_causality: not established; next-hop changes are descriptive only

travel_time.note: Elapsed per-agent decision steps are used for travel time. Global completion timestamps are reported separately and are not mislabeled as individual travel durations.

makespan.note: Team completion makespan is defined only when every navigator completed. Successful-agent makespan is reported separately for partial-completion runs; unfinished agents are right-censored.

task_throughput.definition: Completed navigator goals divided by observed simulation steps. This is a run-level rate, not a per-agent travel speed.

distance.population: All-navigator total is reported only when every navigator has a valid distance; completed-only total is reported only when every completed navigator has a valid distance.
distance.note: Distance is computed from consecutive recorded path nodes using the simulator's geographic edge-distance function when an explicit distance counter is unavailable. Per-agent values may be present even when a population total is incomplete.

sensing_neighborhood_exposure.definition: An agent is counted once per step when a damaged node or disabled edge is in its current-node/one-hop sensing neighbourhood. This is proximity exposure, not physical contact.

severity_weighted_exposure.definition: For each observed agent-step, the maximum node-damage severity in the current node plus one-hop neighbourhood, summed over observed agent-steps. The observed-agent-step mean includes zero-severity observations; the positive-severity mean excludes them. This is a proximity-weighted dose proxy, not a physiological dose or physical-contact measure.

hazard_exposure.severity_weighted_exposure_note: Uses simulator-recorded per-agent, per-step local maximum node damage. Compare only under identical sensing/neighbourhood definitions and simulation horizons.

navigation_association_not_causation.interpretation: Default-policy next-hop changes after information are temporal associations, not causal proof. Planner route changes retain the existing known-blocked-route trigger.

useful_information.raw_read_level_definition: Repeated successful hazard reads are counted; this is access activity, not a count of distinct information acquisitions.
useful_information.usefulness_definition: Unique route-relevant recipient-node acquisitions divided by all unique cross-agent recipient-node acquisitions; deduplicated across shared-memory and local-message channels. Event-level counts are also reported when event mappings exist.
useful_information.interpretation: Route relevance is a snapshot at first cross-agent arrival. Acquisition and novelty are instrumentation proxies, not proof that the agent causally used the information or improved an outcome. Raw repeated reads remain separately available.

communication_efficiency.zero_denominator_policy: Undefined ratios are null, never zero or infinity.

pheromone.interpretation: The no-pheromone counterfactual holds the candidate set and selection temperature fixed and removes only the pheromone score term. Argmax changes show direct score-ranking influence; probability effects quantify the change in candidate selection probability. These are per-decision policy counterfactuals, not a substitute for the paired pheromone-off experiment.

scaling_efficiency.note: A single run cannot establish scaling efficiency. Compare matched workloads at multiple agent counts, then compute throughput(N)/[N * throughput(1)] or an explicitly chosen speedup/efficiency measure across those runs.

definitions.planner_success: A known event hazard invalidates the active route, a replacement plan is found, and the active route changes.
definitions.default_policy_response: A safe next-hop choice after event awareness. This is descriptive and does not establish causal route change.

travel_time.note: Elapsed per-agent decision steps are used for travel time. Global completion timestamps are reported separately and are not mislabeled as individual travel durations.

makespan.note: Team completion makespan is defined only when every navigator completed. Successful-agent makespan is reported separately for partial-completion runs; unfinished agents are right-censored.

task_throughput.definition: Completed navigator goals divided by observed simulation steps. This is a run-level rate, not a per-agent travel speed.

distance.population: All-navigator total is reported only when every navigator has a valid distance; completed-only total is reported only when every completed navigator has a valid distance.
distance.note: Distance is computed from consecutive recorded path nodes using the simulator's geographic edge-distance function when an explicit distance counter is unavailable. Per-agent values may be present even when a population total is incomplete.

sensing_neighborhood_exposure.definition: An agent is counted once per step when a damaged node or disabled edge is in its current-node/one-hop sensing neighbourhood. This is proximity exposure, not physical contact.

severity_weighted_exposure.definition: For each observed agent-step, the maximum node-damage severity in the current node plus one-hop neighbourhood, summed over observed agent-steps. The observed-agent-step mean includes zero-severity observations; the positive-severity mean excludes them. This is a proximity-weighted dose proxy, not a physiological dose or physical-contact measure.

hazard_exposure.severity_weighted_exposure_note: Uses simulator-recorded per-agent, per-step local maximum node damage. Compare only under identical sensing/neighbourhood definitions and simulation horizons.

navigation_association_not_causation.interpretation: Default-policy next-hop changes after information are temporal associations, not causal proof. Planner route changes retain the existing known-blocked-route trigger.

useful_information.raw_read_level_definition: Repeated successful hazard reads are counted; this is access activity, not a count of distinct information acquisitions.
useful_information.usefulness_definition: Unique route-relevant recipient-node acquisitions divided by all unique cross-agent recipient-node acquisitions; deduplicated across shared-memory and local-message channels. Event-level counts are also reported when event mappings exist.
useful_information.interpretation: Route relevance is a snapshot at first cross-agent arrival. Acquisition and novelty are instrumentation proxies, not proof that the agent causally used the information or improved an outcome. Raw repeated reads remain separately available.

communication_efficiency.zero_denominator_policy: Undefined ratios are null, never zero or infinity.

pheromone.interpretation: The no-pheromone counterfactual holds the candidate set and selection temperature fixed and removes only the pheromone score term. scaling_efficiency.note: A single run cannot establish scaling efficiency. Compare matched workloads at multiple agent counts, then compute throughput(N)/[N * throughput(1)] or an explicitly chosen speedup/efficiency measure across those runs.

makespan.note: Team completion makespan is defined only when every navigator completed. Successful-agent makespan is reported separately for partial-completion runs; unfinished agents are right-censored.

task_throughput.definition: Completed navigator goals divided by observed simulation steps. This is a run-level rate, not a per-agent travel speed.

distance.population: All-navigator total is reported only when every navigator has a valid distance; completed-only total is reported only when every completed navigator has a valid distance.
distance.note: Distance is computed from consecutive recorded path nodes using the simulator's geographic edge-distance function when an explicit distance counter is unavailable. Per-agent values may be present even when a population total is incomplete.

sensing_neighborhood_exposure.definition: An agent is counted once per step when a damaged node or disabled edge is in its current-node/one-hop sensing neighbourhood. This is proximity exposure, not physical contact.

severity_weighted_exposure.definition: For each observed agent-step, the maximum node-damage severity in the current node plus one-hop neighbourhood, summed over observed agent-steps. The observed-agent-step mean includes zero-severity observations; the positive-severity mean excludes them. This is a proximity-weighted dose proxy, not a physiological dose or physical-contact measure.

hazard_exposure.severity_weighted_exposure_note: Uses simulator-recorded per-agent, per-step local maximum node damage. Compare only under identical sensing/neighbourhood definitions and simulation horizons.

navigation_association_not_causation.interpretation: Default-policy next-hop changes after information are temporal associations, not causal proof. Planner route changes retain the existing known-blocked-route trigger.

useful_information.raw_read_level_definition: Repeated successful hazard reads are counted; this is access activity, not a count of distinct information acquisitions.
useful_information.usefulness_definition: Unique route-relevant recipient-node acquisitions divided by all unique cross-agent recipient-node acquisitions; deduplicated across shared-memory and local-message channels. Event-level counts are also reported when event mappings exist.
useful_information.interpretation: Route relevance is a snapshot at first cross-agent arrival. Acquisition and novelty are instrumentation proxies, not proof that the agent causally used the information or improved an outcome. Raw repeated reads remain separately available.

communication_efficiency.zero_denominator_policy: Undefined ratios are null, never zero or infinity.

pheromone.interpretation: The no-pheromone counterfactual holds the candidate set and selection temperature fixed and removes only the pheromone score term. Argmax changes show direct score-ranking influence; probability effects quantify the change in candidate selection probability. These are per-decision policy counterfactuals, not a substitute for the paired pheromone-off experiment.

scaling_efficiency.note: A single run cannot establish scaling efficiency. Compare matched workloads at multiple agent counts, then compute throughput(N)/[N * throughput(1)] or an explicitly chosen speedup/efficiency measure across those runs.

The observed-agent-step mean includes zero-severity observations; the positive-severity mean excludes them. hazard_exposure.severity_weighted_exposure_note: Uses simulator-recorded per-agent, per-step local maximum node damage. Compare only under identical sensing/neighbourhood definitions and simulation horizons.

navigation_association_not_causation.interpretation: Default-policy next-hop changes after information are temporal associations, not causal proof. Planner route changes retain the existing known-blocked-route trigger.

useful_information.raw_read_level_definition: Repeated successful hazard reads are counted; this is access activity, not a count of distinct information acquisitions.
useful_information.usefulness_definition: Unique route-relevant recipient-node acquisitions divided by all unique cross-agent recipient-node acquisitions; deduplicated across shared-memory and local-message channels. Event-level counts are also reported when event mappings exist.
useful_information.interpretation: Route relevance is a snapshot at first cross-agent arrival. Acquisition and novelty are instrumentation proxies, not proof that the agent causally used the information or improved an outcome. Raw repeated reads remain separately available.

communication_efficiency.zero_denominator_policy: Undefined ratios are null, never zero or infinity.

pheromone.interpretation: The no-pheromone counterfactual holds the candidate set and selection temperature fixed and removes only the pheromone score term. scaling_efficiency.note: A single run cannot establish scaling efficiency. Compare matched workloads at multiple agent counts, then compute throughput(N)/[N * throughput(1)] or an explicitly chosen speedup/efficiency measure across those runs.

sensing_neighborhood_exposure.definition: An agent is counted once per step when a damaged node or disabled edge is in its current-node/one-hop sensing neighbourhood. This is proximity exposure, not physical contact.

definitions.affected_agent: At event time, the event intersects the agent's active planner route or its current node/local adjacent nodes.
definitions.response_scope: Affected-pair response coverage counts only agents in the initial affected_agent set for each event. definitions.response_delay_scope: mean_response_delay_steps and mean_response_delay_all_agents_steps average all recorded responses. definitions.awareness_source_counts: Counts first-awareness records by their recorded source (for example self_observation, teammate_message, or shared_memory). Counts are records, not unique agents.
definitions.awareness: First recorded self-observation, teammate-message delivery, or successful cross-agent shared-memory hazard lookup containing a node attributed to the event.
definitions.planner_success: A known event hazard invalidates the active route, a replacement plan is found, and the active route changes.

response_metrics.default_policy_route_change_causality: not established; next-hop changes are descriptive only

travel_time.note: Elapsed per-agent decision steps are used for travel time. Global completion timestamps are reported separately and are not mislabeled as individual travel durations.

makespan.note: Team completion makespan is defined only when every navigator completed. Successful-agent makespan is reported separately for partial-completion runs; unfinished agents are right-censored.

task_throughput.definition: Completed navigator goals divided by observed simulation steps. This is a run-level rate, not a per-agent travel speed.

distance.population: All-navigator total is reported only when every navigator has a valid distance; completed-only total is reported only when every completed navigator has a valid distance.
distance.note: Distance is computed from consecutive recorded path nodes using the simulator's geographic edge-distance function when an explicit distance counter is unavailable. Per-agent values may be present even when a population total is incomplete.

sensing_neighborhood_exposure.definition: An agent is counted once per step when a damaged node or disabled edge is in its current-node/one-hop sensing neighbourhood. This is proximity exposure, not physical contact.

severity_weighted_exposure.definition: For each observed agent-step, the maximum node-damage severity in the current node plus one-hop neighbourhood, summed over observed agent-steps. The observed-agent-step mean includes zero-severity observations; the positive-severity mean excludes them. This is a proximity-weighted dose proxy, not a physiological dose or physical-contact measure.

hazard_exposure.severity_weighted_exposure_note: Uses simulator-recorded per-agent, per-step local maximum node damage. Compare only under identical sensing/neighbourhood definitions and simulation horizons.

navigation_association_not_causation.interpretation: Default-policy next-hop changes after information are temporal associations, not causal proof. Planner route changes retain the existing known-blocked-route trigger.

useful_information.raw_read_level_definition: Repeated successful hazard reads are counted; this is access activity, not a count of distinct information acquisitions.

useful_information.interpretation: Route relevance is a snapshot at first cross-agent arrival. Acquisition and novelty are instrumentation proxies, not proof that the agent causally used the information or improved an outcome. Raw repeated reads remain separately available.

communication_efficiency.zero_denominator_policy: Undefined ratios are null, never zero or infinity.

pheromone.interpretation: The no-pheromone counterfactual holds the candidate set and selection temperature fixed and removes only the pheromone score term. definitions.edge_attribution: The engine reports exact edge IDs. Older/custom event providers may fall back to a single-event graph diff; ambiguous simultaneous-event attribution is omitted.

response_metrics.default_policy_route_change_causality: not established; next-hop changes are descriptive only

travel_time.note: Elapsed per-agent decision steps are used for travel time. Global completion timestamps are reported separately and are not mislabeled as individual travel durations.

makespan.note: Team completion makespan is defined only when every navigator completed. Successful-agent makespan is reported separately for partial-completion runs; unfinished agents are right-censored.

task_throughput.definition: Completed navigator goals divided by observed simulation steps. This is a run-level rate, not a per-agent travel speed.

distance.population: All-navigator total is reported only when every navigator has a valid distance; completed-only total is reported only when every completed navigator has a valid distance.
distance.note: Distance is computed from consecutive recorded path nodes using the simulator's geographic edge-distance function when an explicit distance counter is unavailable. Per-agent values may be present even when a population total is incomplete.

sensing_neighborhood_exposure.definition: An agent is counted once per step when a damaged node or disabled edge is in its current-node/one-hop sensing neighbourhood. This is proximity exposure, not physical contact.

severity_weighted_exposure.definition: For each observed agent-step, the maximum node-damage severity in the current node plus one-hop neighbourhood, summed over observed agent-steps. The observed-agent-step mean includes zero-severity observations; the positive-severity mean excludes them. This is a proximity-weighted dose proxy, not a physiological dose or physical-contact measure.

hazard_exposure.severity_weighted_exposure_note: Uses simulator-recorded per-agent, per-step local maximum node damage. Compare only under identical sensing/neighbourhood definitions and simulation horizons.

navigation_association_not_causation.interpretation: Default-policy next-hop changes after information are temporal associations, not causal proof. Planner route changes retain the existing known-blocked-route trigger.

useful_information.raw_read_level_definition: Repeated successful hazard reads are counted; this is access activity, not a count of distinct information acquisitions.
useful_information.usefulness_definition: Unique route-relevant recipient-node acquisitions divided by all unique cross-agent recipient-node acquisitions; deduplicated across shared-memory and local-message channels. Event-level counts are also reported when event mappings exist.
useful_information.interpretation: Route relevance is a snapshot at first cross-agent arrival. Acquisition and novelty are instrumentation proxies, not proof that the agent causally used the information or improved an outcome. Raw repeated reads remain separately available.

communication_efficiency.zero_denominator_policy: Undefined ratios are null, never zero or infinity.

pheromone.interpretation: The no-pheromone counterfactual holds the candidate set and selection temperature fixed and removes only the pheromone score term. Argmax changes show direct score-ranking influence; probability effects quantify the change in candidate selection probability. These are per-decision policy counterfactuals, not a substitute for the paired pheromone-off experiment.

scaling_efficiency.note: A single run cannot establish scaling efficiency. Compare matched workloads at multiple agent counts, then compute throughput(N)/[N * throughput(1)] or an explicitly chosen speedup/efficiency measure across those runs.

definitions.affected_agent: At event time, the event intersects the agent's active planner route or its current node/local adjacent nodes.
definitions.response_scope: Affected-pair response coverage counts only agents in the initial affected_agent set for each event. Responses from agents who learn later through communication or shared memory are counted separately as outside-initial-affected-set responses; they still count in total successful_responses.
definitions.response_delay_scope: mean_response_delay_steps and mean_response_delay_all_agents_steps average all recorded responses. The affected_pairs and outside_initial_affected_set keys report those populations separately. Delay is measured from that agent's first recorded awareness of the event.
definitions.awareness_delay_scope: mean_awareness_delay_steps remains the legacy mean for initially affected agent-event pairs. The explicit all_agents and outside_initial_affected_set fields include later-informed agents. Delays are averaged only over raw records with a non-null awareness_delay_steps value.
definitions.awareness_source_counts: Counts first-awareness records by their recorded source (for example self_observation, teammate_message, or shared_memory). Counts are records, not unique agents.
definitions.awareness: First recorded self-observation, teammate-message delivery, or successful cross-agent shared-memory hazard lookup containing a node attributed to the event.
definitions.planner_success: A known event hazard invalidates the active route, a replacement plan is found, and the active route changes.
definitions.default_policy_response: A safe next-hop choice after event awareness. This is descriptive and does not establish causal route change.
definitions.edge_attribution: The engine reports exact edge IDs. Older/custom event providers may fall back to a single-event graph diff; ambiguous simultaneous-event attribution is omitted.

response_metrics.default_policy_route_change_causality: not established; next-hop changes are descriptive only

travel_time.note: Elapsed per-agent decision steps are used for travel time. Global completion timestamps are reported separately and are not mislabeled as individual travel durations.

makespan.note: Team completion makespan is defined only when every navigator completed. Successful-agent makespan is reported separately for partial-completion runs; unfinished agents are right-censored.

task_throughput.definition: Completed navigator goals divided by observed simulation steps. This is a run-level rate, not a per-agent travel speed.

distance.population: All-navigator total is reported only when every navigator has a valid distance; completed-only total is reported only when every completed navigator has a valid distance.
distance.note: Distance is computed from consecutive recorded path nodes using the simulator's geographic edge-distance function when an explicit distance counter is unavailable. Per-agent values may be present even when a population total is incomplete.

sensing_neighborhood_exposure.definition: An agent is counted once per step when a damaged node or disabled edge is in its current-node/one-hop sensing neighbourhood. This is proximity exposure, not physical contact.

severity_weighted_exposure.definition: For each observed agent-step, the maximum node-damage severity in the current node plus one-hop neighbourhood, summed over observed agent-steps. The observed-agent-step mean includes zero-severity observations; the positive-severity mean excludes them. This is a proximity-weighted dose proxy, not a physiological dose or physical-contact measure.

hazard_exposure.severity_weighted_exposure_note: Uses simulator-recorded per-agent, per-step local maximum node damage. Compare only under identical sensing/neighbourhood definitions and simulation horizons.

navigation_association_not_causation.interpretation: Default-policy next-hop changes after information are temporal associations, not causal proof. Planner route changes retain the existing known-blocked-route trigger.

useful_information.raw_read_level_definition: Repeated successful hazard reads are counted; this is access activity, not a count of distinct information acquisitions.
useful_information.usefulness_definition: Unique route-relevant recipient-node acquisitions divided by all unique cross-agent recipient-node acquisitions; deduplicated across shared-memory and local-message channels. Event-level counts are also reported when event mappings exist.
useful_information.interpretation: Route relevance is a snapshot at first cross-agent arrival. Acquisition and novelty are instrumentation proxies, not proof that the agent causally used the information or improved an outcome. Raw repeated reads remain separately available.

communication_efficiency.zero_denominator_policy: Undefined ratios are null, never zero or infinity.

pheromone.interpretation: The no-pheromone counterfactual holds the candidate set and selection temperature fixed and removes only the pheromone score term. Argmax changes show direct score-ranking influence; probability effects quantify the change in candidate selection probability. These are per-decision policy counterfactuals, not a substitute for the paired pheromone-off experiment.

scaling_efficiency.note: A single run cannot establish scaling efficiency. Compare matched workloads at multiple agent counts, then compute throughput(N)/[N * throughput(1)] or an explicitly chosen speedup/efficiency measure across those runs.

Responses from agents who learn later through communication or shared memory are counted separately as outside-initial-affected-set responses; they still count in total successful_responses.
definitions.response_delay_scope: mean_response_delay_steps and mean_response_delay_all_agents_steps average all recorded responses. The affected_pairs and outside_initial_affected_set keys report those populations separately. Delay is measured from that agent's first recorded awareness of the event.
definitions.awareness_delay_scope: mean_awareness_delay_steps remains the legacy mean for initially affected agent-event pairs. The explicit all_agents and outside_initial_affected_set fields include later-informed agents. Delays are averaged only over raw records with a non-null awareness_delay_steps value.
definitions.awareness_source_counts: Counts first-awareness records by their recorded source (for example self_observation, teammate_message, or shared_memory). Counts are records, not unique agents.
definitions.awareness: First recorded self-observation, teammate-message delivery, or successful cross-agent shared-memory hazard lookup containing a node attributed to the event.
definitions.planner_success: A known event hazard invalidates the active route, a replacement plan is found, and the active route changes.
definitions.default_policy_response: A safe next-hop choice after event awareness. This is descriptive and does not establish causal route change.
definitions.edge_attribution: The engine reports exact edge IDs. Older/custom event providers may fall back to a single-event graph diff; ambiguous simultaneous-event attribution is omitted.

response_metrics.default_policy_route_change_causality: not established; next-hop changes are descriptive only

travel_time.note: Elapsed per-agent decision steps are used for travel time. Global completion timestamps are reported separately and are not mislabeled as individual travel durations.

makespan.note: Team completion makespan is defined only when every navigator completed. Successful-agent makespan is reported separately for partial-completion runs; unfinished agents are right-censored.

task_throughput.definition: Completed navigator goals divided by observed simulation steps. This is a run-level rate, not a per-agent travel speed.

distance.population: All-navigator total is reported only when every navigator has a valid distance; completed-only total is reported only when every completed navigator has a valid distance.
distance.note: Distance is computed from consecutive recorded path nodes using the simulator's geographic edge-distance function when an explicit distance counter is unavailable. Per-agent values may be present even when a population total is incomplete.

sensing_neighborhood_exposure.definition: An agent is counted once per step when a damaged node or disabled edge is in its current-node/one-hop sensing neighbourhood. This is proximity exposure, not physical contact.

severity_weighted_exposure.definition: For each observed agent-step, the maximum node-damage severity in the current node plus one-hop neighbourhood, summed over observed agent-steps. The observed-agent-step mean includes zero-severity observations; the positive-severity mean excludes them. This is a proximity-weighted dose proxy, not a physiological dose or physical-contact measure.

hazard_exposure.severity_weighted_exposure_note: Uses simulator-recorded per-agent, per-step local maximum node damage. Compare only under identical sensing/neighbourhood definitions and simulation horizons.

navigation_association_not_causation.interpretation: Default-policy next-hop changes after information are temporal associations, not causal proof. Planner route changes retain the existing known-blocked-route trigger.

useful_information.raw_read_level_definition: Repeated successful hazard reads are counted; this is access activity, not a count of distinct information acquisitions.
useful_information.usefulness_definition: Unique route-relevant recipient-node acquisitions divided by all unique cross-agent recipient-node acquisitions; deduplicated across shared-memory and local-message channels. Event-level counts are also reported when event mappings exist.
useful_information.interpretation: Route relevance is a snapshot at first cross-agent arrival. Acquisition and novelty are instrumentation proxies, not proof that the agent causally used the information or improved an outcome. Raw repeated reads remain separately available.

communication_efficiency.zero_denominator_policy: Undefined ratios are null, never zero or infinity.

pheromone.interpretation: The no-pheromone counterfactual holds the candidate set and selection temperature fixed and removes only the pheromone score term. Argmax changes show direct score-ranking influence; probability effects quantify the change in candidate selection probability. These are per-decision policy counterfactuals, not a substitute for the paired pheromone-off experiment.

scaling_efficiency.note: A single run cannot establish scaling efficiency. Compare matched workloads at multiple agent counts, then compute throughput(N)/[N * throughput(1)] or an explicitly chosen speedup/efficiency measure across those runs.

instrumentation_notes.coverage: Exact visited node-ID sets and cell-count keys.
instrumentation_notes.awareness: One first-awareness record per agent-event pair.
instrumentation_notes.early_warning: Censored if the agent never independently discovers the event.
instrumentation_notes.travel_time: Per-agent decision steps for completed navigators; global completion timestamps reported separately.
instrumentation_notes.makespan: Team completion makespan is null unless all navigators complete; partial successful makespan and observed horizon are separate.
